did_you_know.text: The prophecy begins with the phrase “And afterward,” indicating that the outpouring of the Spirit is described as an event that will occur after an earlier stage.
The phrase “on all flesh” presents the Spirit of the LORD as a gift not limited to one small group.

The verse mentions sons and daughters, old men and young men together, and attributes prophecy, dreams, or visions to them—without distinguishing between women and men or between the young and the old.
Male and female servants are also explicitly included in the outpouring of the Spirit of the LORD, emphasizing that social status does not prevent anyone from receiving the Spirit.
The signs described in the prophecy appear both in the heavens and on the earth, including blood, fire, and pillars of smoke.
The verse describes a change in the heavenly lights: the sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of “the great and awesome day of the LORD.”

Deliverance is connected with calling on the name of the LORD: everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape. Mount Zion and Jerusalem are also mentioned as places where there will be deliverance.
At the end of the passage, “the survivors whom the LORD calls” are mentioned; that is, the verse also connects deliverance with the LORD’s call and with those who respond to it.
